chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, who said:
The waiting period of the non-Muslim woman (Al-Ajlaja) when she becomes a Muslim is the waiting period of the divorced woman, when she intends to marry someone else.

key_terms.الْعِلْجَةِ: The non-Muslim woman (specifically from the People of the Book), derived from 'Ajlaj'
key_terms.عِدَّةُ: Waiting period (Iddah) after divorce or death

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a non-Muslim woman who converts to Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies that a non-Muslim woman (Ahl al-Zimma) who converts to Islam while her husband remains non-Muslim does not await his conversion but instead observes the *Iddah* of a divorced woman (three menstrual cycles). This ruling, derived from the principle of *Faraq* (separation) upon conversion, ensures her legal status is clear for remarriage, distinguishing it from the waiting period for widows. It highlights the Shia juristic view that conversion severs the marital bond immediately, requiring a distinct waiting period to confirm non-pregnancy and finalize the separation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus,
‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A waiting period of the الْعِلْجَةِ when she becomes a Muslim, is a waiting period of the divorced woman, when she intends to marry someone else’.
